content:
Over the past year, we've been looking forward to the next-generation iPad mini update, and it looks like the new device is about to launch. Last week, Aaron Perris revealed that the new device will feature an A20 Pro chip and narrower bezels, and we also know it will use an OLED screen and have a waterproof design.

While these upgrades are impressive, I have one biggest expectation for the next iPad mini, and it's about software.

After watching iPhone Duo, I was amazed at how well Apple handles multitasking. Multitasking on iPad has always felt chaotic to me, but iPhone Duo feels elegant.

On such a small screen, window management on the iPad mini has never really worked well. Users rarely overlap multiple windows on the iPad mini. So I hope Apple can take a page from iPhone Duo: split view plus picture-in-picture.

Hot comments posted by Mathew Ledbetter

Well said, similar to my biggest complaint; the software is just a shrunken version of the larger iPad. Apple hasn't put much thought into adjusting the experience for this size. Widgets are too small. The number of icon rows on the home screen is extremely limited, wasting a lot of space. It's a really poor experience.

Honestly, this experience is really good. Currently on the iPad mini, in portrait mode, there's no way to stretch a picture-in-picture window to fill the full width of the device, and even if you could, you'd either block part of the app or have to manually resize using the window feature.

For me, bringing split-screen video and app viewing to the iPad mini's screen is simply a given, especially since the aspect ratios of the iPhone Duo and iPad mini screens are so similar. At least personally, if this feature existed, I would use the iPad mini in portrait mode more often.
